# Standards

Team-wide rules. One place, one version, referenced everywhere else.

| File | What it settles |
|---|---|
| [`naming-conventions.md`](naming-conventions.md) | What we call workspaces, items, branches, folders |
| [`branching-and-workspaces.md`](branching-and-workspaces.md) | Which branch maps to which workspace, and how work flows between them |
| [`review-checklist.md`](review-checklist.md) | What a reviewer actually checks before approving |
| [`security-and-access.md`](security-and-access.md) | Who gets access to what, and where secrets live |
| [`glossary.md`](glossary.md) | Domain terms — the vocabulary agents and humans share |

## How to change a standard

These files are the reason the repo stays coherent, so they change by pull request, not in passing.

1. Open a PR that changes the standard **and** the things it affects.
2. Say what breaks. A naming change that isn't applied to existing items is worse than no change.
3. Get one reviewer outside your project. Standards that only serve one team aren't standards.
